observation.visible_scene: A green felt pool table set against a peach-colored wall, with a padded bench/chair and a small side table visible in the blurred background. A blue-and-white striped '10' ball rests near the center of the table, and a large out-of-focus white cue ball occupies the bottom-left foreground.
visible_changes: For the first ~0.3 s the striped 10-ball and the foreground cue ball remain essentially stationary.

Around t=0.4–0.5 s the foreground cue ball moves sharply into the mid-ground (becoming in-focus) and a wooden cue stick enters from the left; the cue ball reaches the 10-ball and the two overlap, indicating contact.
After contact the striped 10-ball translates leftward across the table, from center (≈x=525) to near the left rail (≈x=210) over t≈0.5–1.0 s.
The white cue ball continues to the right, grows blurry and smaller, and exits the right edge of frame by t≈0.8 s.
The cue stick retracts and leaves the frame after t≈0.6 s.
From t≈1.0 s to the end the 10-ball no longer translates; it stays parked at the left rail and only rotates in place (the stripe/number orientation changes frame to frame).
The background furniture and wall stay at fixed positions throughout, indicating a largely static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The player, the stroke that launched the cue ball, and any pocket or final resting position of the cue ball are not shown.
Whether the 10-ball eventually drops into a side pocket or stays put is beyond the clip's end.
What preceded the cue ball's foreground position (its own prior motion) is unseen.
uncertain_details: The cue ball's path after contact looks slightly elevated/blurry, so it is unclear whether it briefly hops or simply rolls fast.
The exact moment of ball-to-ball contact is between sampled frames (visible around t=0.47–0.53 s).
The 10-ball's late motion is interpreted as spin-in-place; small residual drift cannot be ruled out at this frame rate.
